text: I'm Lieutenant Jim McAndrew from the Secretary of the Air Force Classification and Review Team,
and we've been asked to look into an incident by the GAO for the Secretary of the Air Force,
a GAO investigation revolving around something called the Roswell incident
that's been highly publicized.
There's been books written on it, movies, newspaper articles, things like that.
and we've come through our investigation, we've come to believe that they're describing an event that you participated in in 1959.
You were a physician at the Walker Air Force Base Hospital in Roswell, New Mexico.
I guess I'd just like to start off with asking you, when did you join the Air Force, and when were you at Walker Air Force Base?
My name is Charles A. Coltman, Jr., M.D., Colonel, USAF, M.C., retired. I entered the United States Air Force on 13 September 1977 and retired on that date in 1957.
and retired 20 years later in 1977.

Yeah, I left.

Yes.

1957 to that date in 1977 when I retired from the United States Air Force.
Okay. What was your, during your Air Force career, what major jobs did you hold?
I was, had three PCS assignments. One was as a flight surgeon at Walker Air Force Base,
Roswell, New Mexico from 1957 to 1959. The second was... Do you remember the month in 1959?
That I left? It was in July that I left. Okay. All right. June or July. It was somewhere like that.
And then I left there and was an Air Force-sponsored resident at Ohio State University from 1959 to 1963.
And I finished my residency and then was PCS to Wilford Hall USAF Medical Center in San Antonio, Texas,
where I spent 14 years as various jobs as staff hematologist, chief of hematology
oncology service, and chairman of the Department of Medicine. I retired from
the United States Air Force in 1977 and joined the faculty at the University of
Texas Health Science Center in San Antonio and I've been jointly working at
at the university and at the cancer therapy and research center since that time.
Okay. All right. So the particular time we're interested in is the time when there was an incident at Walker Air Force, near Walker Air Force Base, and it was in May of 1959, May 21, 1959.

Sergeant Wormwood, who was the NCOIC of the Flight Surgeon's Office, and he said,
balloon accident north of Roswell and we need to go investigate it." And I thought
he was kidding me and hung up on him. He immediately called back and said,

and Sergeant Wormwood came by in the big blue cracker box ambulance,

who were sitting on the ground next to it.

to me. And so I called and he was anxious to get them back to Holloman. I described

went back to Holloman. My memory about what happened after that is somewhat remote, but
